## About

This repository contains the official preview container images for Azure Linux 4.0. To learn more about Azure Linux container images, see our container [documentation](https://aka.ms/azurelinux-containers).

### What is Azure Linux?

Azure Linux is a Microsoft-maintained, open-source Linux distribution built for Azure. It provides a lightweight, security-hardened operating system for virtual machines (VMs), containers, and Kubernetes clusters running on Azure infrastructure. 

To learn more about Azure Linux, refer to our [documentation](https://www.aka.ms/azurelinux).

## Images

The following images are available:

| Image             | Tags     |
| ----------------- | -------- |
| `mcr.microsoft.com/azurelinux-beta/base/core`          | `4.0` |
| `mcr.microsoft.com/azurelinux-beta/distroless/minimal` | `4.0` |
| `mcr.microsoft.com/azurelinux-beta/distroless/base`    | `4.0` |
| `mcr.microsoft.com/azurelinux-beta/distroless/debug`   | `4.0` |

## Usage
### Standard Container
To use our container, run:

`docker run -it --rm mcr.microsoft.com/azurelinux-beta/base/core:4.0`

The default container startup command is `bash`.

### Distroless Container
Distroless containers contain only the minimal set of packages your application needs, with anything extra removed (i.e. package manager, libraries and shell).

Due to their limited set of packages, distroless containers have a minimized security attack surface as well as reduced noise from vulnerability scanners. This generally translates to a reduced overhead of patching vulnerabilities, allowing developers to focus on building their application.

#### Minimal
The `minimal` image is the smallest distroless image. It is primarily intended for use with golang or other statically linked applications.

#### Base
The `base` image adds the core Azure Linux packages to the minimal image. It is primarily intended for C based applications.

#### Debug
The `debug` image adds the busybox package to the base image to provide a lightweight debugging environment.

`docker run -it --rm mcr.microsoft.com/azurelinux-beta/distroless/debug:4.0 busybox sh`

#### Docker multi-stage build
Using Docker’s multi-stage build provides an easy way to use distroless images. The basic idea is that you'll have one stage to build your application artifacts or install additional packages and insert them into your runtime distroless image. To learn more, please see the documentation on [multi-stage builds](https://docs.docker.com/develop/develop-images/multistage-build/).

#### Container image pinning
By default, container images are referenced using floating tags (e.g., `:4.0`).

Tags are intentionally used to:

- Receive automatic updates and security fixes.
- Reduce operational overhead for customers.
- Align with continuously updated base images.

However, tags are mutable and will change over time. For scenarios requiring strict reproducibility or supply chain control, images can optionally be pinned to a specific SHA256 digest as follow:

`<AZURELINUX_MCR_IMAGE>:<TAG>@sha256:<DIGEST>`

Example:

`mcr.microsoft.com/azurelinux-beta/base/core:4.0@sha256:123456789101112`

## Support

Official Azure Support is for production issues only. If you're running an Azure Linux production workload on Azure and you hit an outage, regression, or configuration problem that's affecting that workload, [open an Azure support request](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-portal/supportability/how-to-create-azure-support-request) through the Azure portal.

For more ways to get help, see our [Support options](https://aka.ms/azurelinux-help).
